title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-04
content:
2026-03-04 scratchpad - quick notes + TODOs

Context: running a couple of quantized eval sweeps on candidate open models for reranking baseline. Trying to reproduce low-latency quality characteristics with q8 and q4f16 backends. Focus: short chat-like prompts + rerank prompts (50-200 tokens).

Goals for this week:
- [ ] Finalize baseline prompt set (50 queries) for rerank eval (priority)
- [ ] Run full eval for LLama-2-13b-ggml/q8 -> get pass@1 / nDCG@5 numbers
- [x] Quick smoke runs for q8 (bitsandbytes) to check stability
- [ ] Benchmark latency on dedicated small GPU (A10g) w/ batch=1, seq=128
- [ ] Add prompt-level logging to eval harness (Miguel)

Latest experiment notes:
- Run: quick-smoke-q8-2026-03-03
  - Model: llama-2-13b-v2 (hf-copy) -> quantized with bitsandbytes 8-bit (q8_0)
  - Eval harness: local eval script (eval/rerank_eval.py)
  - Prompt set: small-rerank-20.json (dev)
  - Results (approx): nDCG@5 = 0.62, MRR = 0.48. Roughly -3% vs fp16 baseline on same prompt set.
  - Latency (p50 token gen): 18ms/token (seq=128, batch=1) on A10g emulated env -> seems reasonable.
  - Failure modes: occasional decoder explosion when using causal padding strategy in our runtime tests (Sam observed stack traces).

Notes on quantization config tried:
- q8_0 via bitsandbytes (default): good memory reduction, minor quality drop on rerank set
- q4f16 (experimental): ran single test, observed more quality degradation (~7% nDCG drop) but uses less VRAM. Need to check calibration / per-channel minima.
- Post-training quantization: using GPTQ-lite gave slightly better quality than naive q4 but slower inference in our runtime due to kernel mismatch.

Prompts (examples used in rerank eval):
- Prompt A (short instruction): "Rank these candidate answers by usefulness for the query: {query}
Candidates:
1) {cand1}
2) {cand2}
3) {cand3}
Answer: "
- Prompt B (chat style): "User: {query}
Assistant: You are an expert assistant. Rank the following candidate replies from best to worst and explain briefly.
Candidates:
- A: {cand1}
- B: {cand2}
- C: {cand3}
Ranking:"

Quick commands I ran (notes):
- export HF_TOKEN=***; python eval/rerank_eval.py --model hf://llama-2-13b-v2 --quant q8_0 --prompts data/small-rerank-20.json --out results/q8-smoke-20260303.json
- python bench/latency.py --model local:q8-llama-13b --seq 128 --batch 1 --gpu A10g

Open questions / TODO for next session:
- Is bitsandbytes q8_0 compatible with our runtime kernels for continuous batching? (Sam to check kernel fusing)
- Re-run q4f16 with per-channel scale calibration (try GPTQ exported scales) to see if gap closes
- Add one-shot prompt variants to the prompt set (we currently only test zero-shot)
- Get full 50-query rerank eval and compare to fp16 baseline (need GPU hours, request from infra)

Quick debugging notes (from Sam):
- Decoder overflow happens when using attention-cache shrink optimization + q8 in the combined path. Suspect KV cache alignment bug. Repro minimal script: runtest/kv-cache-align.py --model q8-llama-13b --steps 80

Reference links / artifacts:
- PR with quantization helpers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/llm-runtime/pull/342 (Miguel)
- Jira ticket tracking infra quota: ENG-1287

Scratch TODO (short):
- [ ] Add 50-query prompt file (small-rerank-50.json) -> convert from internal rerank-suite
- [ ] Tag runs with commit hash in results metadata (easy fix in eval harness)
- [ ] Try q8na (new q8 variant) when Miguel lands perf patches

End of scratchpad. Keep brief, iterate tomorrow.
